knowledge_graph.description: Cancer Medicine is a monthly peer-reviewed open-access medical journal covering oncology. It was established in 2012 and is published by John Wiley & Sons. The editor-in-chief is Stephen Tait. According to the Journal Citation Reports, the journal has a 2020 impact factor of 4.452.

related_questions.snippet: Chemotherapy drugs destroy fast-growing cells in the body. The goal is to lower the total number of cancer cells in your body and reduce the chances that the cancer will spread (metastasize). If you have curable cancer, chemo may even be used to cure it.

text_blocks.snippet: There are many different types of cancer medicines, with various brand names and generic names. Some examples include Keytruda (pembrolizumab), Gemzar (gemcitabine), and Doxil (doxorubicin hydrochloride liposome). These drugs can be used to treat a wide range of cancers.

list.snippet: Keytruda (pembrolizumab): A type of immunotherapy that helps the body's immune system fight cancer cells.
Gemzar (gemcitabine): A chemotherapy drug used to treat various cancers.
Doxil (doxorubicin hydrochloride liposome): A chemotherapy drug, specifically a type of anthracycline, used in treating certain cancers.
Cyclophosphamide: A chemotherapy drug often used in treating various cancers.
Doxorubicin: Another anthracycline chemotherapy drug, used to treat a wide range of cancers.
Gleevec (imatinib mesylate): A targeted therapy used to treat certain types of leukemia and gastrointestinal stromal tumors.
Herceptin (trastuzumab): A targeted therapy used to treat certain types of breast and stomach cancers.
Avastin (bevacizumab): A targeted therapy used in treating various cancers.
Rituxan (rituximab): A targeted therapy used to treat certain types of lymphoma and leukemia.

text_blocks.snippet: Cancer treatment drugs encompass a wide range of medications used to target and destroy cancer cells or modulate their growth. Chemotherapy drugs, targeted therapies, hormone therapies, and immunotherapies are among the major categories, each with its own mechanisms and applications. Many drugs are used in combination or with other treatments like radiation therapy.
snippet_highlighted_words: Chemotherapy drugs, targeted therapies, hormone therapies, and immunotherapies

list.title: Mechanism:
list.snippet: Chemotherapy drugs, often referred to as "chemo," interfere with cancer cell division and growth, ultimately killing these cells.

list.title: Types:
list.snippet: Chemotherapy drugs can be broadly classified into:
Alkylating agents: These drugs damage DNA, preventing cancer cells from replicating. Examples include cyclophosphamide, cisplatin, and carboplatin.
Antimetabolites: These drugs interfere with DNA and RNA synthesis, disrupting cell division. Examples include methotrexate, 5-fluorouracil, and gemcitabine.
Antitumor antibiotics: These drugs can damage DNA and inhibit RNA and protein synthesis. Examples include doxorubicin, daunorubicin, and mitoxantrone.
Topoisomerase inhibitors: These drugs interfere with enzymes (topoisomerases) that help unwind and rewind DNA during cell division. Examples include irinotecan and topotecan.
Mitotic inhibitors: These drugs interfere with cell division by disrupting microtubule formation. Examples include vinca alkaloids (vinblastine, vincristine) and taxanes (paclitaxel, docetaxel).

list.title: Administration:
list.snippet: Chemotherapy drugs are often administered intravenously (through a vein) or orally (as pills or capsules).

list.title: Examples:
list.snippet: CMF (Cyclophosphamide, Methotrexate, 5-fluorouracil), AC (Doxorubicin, Cyclophosphamide), ABVD (Doxorubicin, Bleomycin, Vinblastine, Dacarbazine), and BEACOPP (Bleomycin, Etoposide, Doxorubicin, Cyclophosphamide, Vincristine, Procarbazine, Prednisone) are examples of common chemotherapy regimens.

list.title: Mechanism:
list.snippet: Targeted therapies focus on specific molecules or pathways that are crucial for cancer cell growth and survival.

list.title: Types:
list.snippet: These therapies include drugs that block growth factor receptors, inhibit intracellular signaling pathways, or promote cancer cell death.

list.title: Examples:
list.snippet: Trastuzumab (Herceptin), imatinib (Gleevec), and cetuximab (Erbitux) are examples of targeted therapies.

list.title: Mechanism:
list.snippet: These therapies block or lower the levels of hormones that can fuel certain types of cancer (like breast, prostate, and endometrial cancers).

list.title: Examples:
list.snippet: Tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors, and leuprolide are examples of hormone therapies.

list.title: Mechanism:
list.snippet: These therapies help the body's immune system recognize and attack cancer cells.

list.title: Types:
list.snippet: Immunotherapies include checkpoint inhibitors, adoptive cell transfer, and cancer vaccines.

list.title: Examples:
list.snippet: Pembrolizumab (Keytruda), nivolumab (Opdivo), and ipilimumab (Yervoy) are examples of immunotherapies.

list.title: Steroids:
list.snippet: Steroids like dexamethasone, prednisone, and methylprednisolone can be used to manage side effects of chemotherapy, reduce inflammation, and treat certain cancers.

list.title: Bisphosphonates:
list.snippet: Medications like zoledronic acid and pamidronate can help strengthen bones and prevent fractures in patients with bone metastases.

list.title: Bone marrow stimulants:
list.snippet: These medications, such as filgrastim and sargramostim, can help the body produce more blood cells after chemotherapy.

list.title: Drug shortages:
list.snippet: Shortages of certain chemotherapy drugs, like cisplatin and carboplatin, can delay treatment and impact patient care.

text_blocks.snippet: "Cancer med" typically refers to medications used to treat cancer, often called antineoplastic drugs. These medications can be categorized into several types, including chemotherapy, targeted therapy, hormone therapy, and immunotherapy. Each type works differently to target cancer cells and can be used alone or in combination with other treatments.
snippet_highlighted_words: medications used to treat cancer, often called antineoplastic drugs

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at the different types of cancer medications:

list.snippet: Chemotherapy drugs are designed to kill or inhibit the growth of cancer cells.
They work by interfering with cell division and replication, which is a process that cancer cells often utilize at a higher rate than normal cells.
Examples of chemotherapy drugs include: 5-fluorouracil, methotrexate, and cisplatin.
Targeted therapies are designed to specifically target certain molecules or pathways that are involved in cancer cell growth and survival.
They can be more selective than chemotherapy, potentially causing fewer side effects on healthy cells.
Examples of targeted therapies include: tyrosine kinase inhibitors and monoclonal antibodies.
Hormone therapy is used to treat cancers that are sensitive to hormones, such as breast and prostate cancer.
It works by blocking the production of hormones or interfering with their ability to stimulate cancer cell growth.
Examples of hormone therapy drugs include anastrozole and tamoxifen.
Immunotherapy helps the body's own immune system to recognize and attack cancer cells.
This can be achieved through various mechanisms, such as boosting the activity of immune cells or targeting specific molecules on cancer cells.
Examples of immunotherapy include checkpoint inhibitors and CAR T-cell therapy.

list.title: Not all cancer medications are chemotherapy:
list.snippet: It's important to understand that chemotherapy is just one type of cancer treatment, and there are other options available depending on the specific type and stage of cancer.

list.title: Individualized treatment:
list.snippet: The best approach to cancer treatment often involves a combination of different therapies tailored to the individual patient and their specific cancer.

list.title: Side effects:
list.snippet: All cancer treatments can have side effects, and it's crucial to discuss these with your doctor to manage them effectively.
